name: Bronchogen
summary: A four-amino-acid peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the lungs and airways; evidence so far is limited to cell and rat studies.
what_it_is: Bronchogen is a lab-made chain of four amino acids, alanine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid and leucine, developed by Vladimir Khavinson's group in Russia, where it is listed as a dietary supplement. The developer's patent gives the order as Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu (AEDL), while some of the group's papers write Ala-Asp-Glu-Leu. In lab studies it switched on genes used by the cells lining the airways, including genes for mucus and surfactant, the film that keeps the lungs' air sacs open.

evidence.why: Only cell-culture and rat studies were found, almost all from the developer's group; no human trials have been published.

status_us.label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
status_us.note: Bronchogen is not an FDA-approved drug and appears on none of FDA's compounding lists (nominated substances, updated May 2026; safety-risk and withdrawn nominations, April 2026). FDA allows pharmacy compounding only from ingredients that are in an approved drug, meet a USP standard, or are on or under review for its bulk list; Russia's drug register lists it as a dietary supplement.

benefits.claim: Reversed damage to the airway lining and calmed airway inflammation in rats with a COPD-like lung disease
Faster recovery from bacterial lung inflammation, and milder lung scarring after lung injury, in rats
Switched on genes for airway-lining cell maturation, mucus and surfactant in human airway cell cultures

risks.risk: Never tested in people, so side effects in humans are unknown; the developer's animal tests reported no toxicity
No FDA-approved or pharmacy-compounded version exists, so the identity and purity of products are unverified

avoid_if: Asthma, COPD or other lung disease: do not replace prescribed treatment, and talk to a clinician first

before: General health check with a clinician
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for Bronchogen because it has not been studied in people.

studies.title: Modulating Effect of Peptide Therapy on the Morphofunctional State of Bronchial Epithelium in Rats with Obstructive Lung Pathology
studies.people: Rats with COPD-like disease caused by nitrogen dioxide
studies.finding: Treatment with Bronchogen reversed remodeling of the airway lining, restored ciliated cells, raised secretory IgA (a local immune defense) and reduced neutrophil-driven inflammation.

studies.title: Peptide regulation of gene expression and protein synthesis in bronchial epithelium
studies.people: Human embryonic bronchial epithelial cell cultures
studies.finding: The peptide changed markers of cell growth, turned on airway differentiation genes such as NKX2-1, FOXA1 and FOXA2 and mucus and surfactant genes, and appeared to bind DNA in test-tube experiments.

studies.title: Peptide Regulation of Cell Differentiation
studies.finding: A review by the developers reporting that AEDL raised activity of airway-cell genes 1.5 to 2.6 times in human embryonic lung cells.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on the amino-acid order: the developer's US patent 7,625,870 and the group's 2020 and 2021 reviews give Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu (AEDL), while the 2014 Lung paper (whose figures label the peptide 'Bronchogen', seen in the author reprint at khavinson.info) writes Ala-Asp-Glu-Leu (ADEL), as does a PubMed title seen in search results but not opened (PMID 21240358). No human studies were found; all evidence is cell or rat work from the developer's group or collaborators, and the rat lung-injury and fibrosis results come from the patent. Russian supplement status was seen on the RLS register's group listing only (the product page could not be opened).
